title: CVE-2026-123007: Critical NGINX2Root HTTP/2 Flaw Enables Remote Code Execution
content_md: F5 has released emergency security updates addressing CVE-2026-123007, a critical memory-corruption vulnerability in NGINX that can allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute code on vulnerable web servers. Dubbed NGINX2Root , the flaw resides in NGINX’s HTTP/2 flow-control implementation and has been present in the codebase for more than a decade. The vulnerability carries a CVSS v4 score of 9.2 . An attacker who can reach an HTTP/2-enabled NGINX listener can manipulate flow-control state until an invalid response length causes out-of-bounds memory access. Depending on the target environment, exploitation can crash an NGINX worker, disclose memory, corrupt process memory, or enable arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the worker process. NGINX Open Source releases from 1.9.5 through 1.31.8 are vulnerable. F5 released fixed versions 1.30.7 for the stable branch and 1.31.9 for mainline on November 18, 2026. NGINX Plus is also affected across multiple 37.x and older supported branches. The flaw is particularly concerning because authentication is not required. Xint researchers demonstrated remote command execution through a reachable HTTP/2 service, while Rapid7 independently developed an unauthenticated RCE exploit against NGINX 1.31.8. However, obtaining root privileges on the underlying operating system requires a separate privilege-escalation vulnerability or another post-exploitation technique.
